items.prompt: If we’re told how much of a picture fraction is shaded, there’s then a rule to how much is not shaded.
items.demo: The number of parts shaded and number of parts not shaded always sum to *the bottom number* in the symbolic fraction..

items.prompt: So here, there are ten parts in the whole unit.
items.demo: Three parts are shaded. *Seven* parts are not shaded. Three and seven sum to make ten.

items.prompt: Here, there are five parts in the whole unit.
items.demo: One part is shaded. *Four* parts are not shaded. One and four sum to make five.

items.prompt: Finally, here there are six parts in the whole unit.
items.demo: Four parts are shaded. *Two* parts are not shaded. Four and two sum to make six.

items.prompt: So, even without a picture… if I know that two tenths are shaded, then I also know that eight parts are not shaded, because two and eight sum to make ten.
items.demo: *Eight* parts are not shaded, 8/10, because two and eight sum to make ten. (2 + 8)/10

items.prompt: And if I know that three sevenths are NOT shaded, then I also know that four sevenths are shaded, because three and four sum to make seven.
items.demo: *Four sevenths* are shaded, 4/7, because three and four sum to make seven. (3 + 4)/7

items.prompt: Your turn. Two tenths of a picture are shaded 2/10. How many parts are not shaded?
items.demo: *Eight* parts are not shaded, because two and eight sum to make ten.

items.prompt: Seven tenths of a picture are shaded 7/10. How many are not shaded?
items.demo: *Three* parts are not shaded, because seven and three sum to make ten.

items.prompt: Seven tenths of a picture are NOT shaded 7/10. How many are shaded?
items.demo: *Three* parts are shaded, because seven and three sum to make ten.

items.prompt: Three eighths of a picture are shaded 3/8. How many parts are not shaded?
items.demo: *Five* parts are not shaded, because three and five sum to make eight.

items.prompt: Two sixths of a picture are shaded 2/6. How many parts are not shaded?
items.demo: *Four* parts are not shaded, because two and four sum to make six.

items.prompt: Four ninths of a picture are NOT shaded 4/9. How many are shaded?
items.demo: *Five* parts are shaded, because four and five sum to make nine.

items.prompt: Six sevenths of a picture are shaded 6/7. How many are not shaded?
items.demo: *One* part is not shaded, because six and one sum to make seven.

items.prompt: We’re using the letter n to represent an unknown number. If eight twentieths of a picture are shaded 8/20, which of these shows the sum of the shaded and unshaded parts combined?  (8 + 8)/20  12/20  (8 + 12)/20  (12 + 12)/20
items.demo: Eight parts are shaded and twelve parts are not shaded, so the sum of the shaded and unshaded parts is *(8 + 12)/20*.

items.prompt: We’re using the letter n to represent an unknown number. If two fifths of a picture are shaded 2/5 , which of these is true?  2 + n = 5  1 + n = 5  2-n = 5  x-n = 5
items.demo: *2 + n = 5*. The number of parts shaded and number of parts not shaded always sum to the bottom number in the symbolic fraction..

items.prompt: Three parts of a picture fraction are shaded 3/▢. Five parts are not shaded 5/▢. What number goes on the bottom of each symbolic fraction?
items.demo: *Eight*, because three and five sum to make eight.
